proposals.reaction: Rusting: 4Fe + 3O2 + 2H2O -> 2Fe2O3.H2O, dH ~ -824 kJ/mol Fe2O3. Acid attack: Fe + 2HCl -> FeCl2 + H2, dH ~ -88 kJ/mol Fe
proposals.dT_basis: Rusting is the classic slow, near-zero-exotherm corrosion (3K, 0.002 chance = a 'takes years' rate), independent of stock IRON's existing salt-triggered corrosion. Acid dissolution is a visibly faster, more vigorous reaction that fizzes H2 -> higher dT (60K) and chance (0.15), but still well short of a violent alkali-metal reaction.
proposals.note: Stock IRON's description ('Rusts with salt, can be used for electrolysis of WATR') implies a salt/electrolysis-specific native path already exists; this proposal adds the independent plain-water-plus-air rusting path and a distinct acid-attack path with H2 evolution, matching the reaction pattern given in the task brief.
